:::{#def-affine-map}
#### Affine map

A [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function) $f: \mathbb{R}^p \to \mathbb{R}^m$ is an **affine map**
(also called an *affine transformation* or *affine function*)
if it is a matrix product followed by a translation (@def-translation):
there are an $m \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ and a vector $\vec{b} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ such that

$$f(\vx) = t_{\vec{b}}(\matr{A} \vx) = \matr{A} \vx + \vec{b} \quad \text{for all } \vx \in \mathbb{R}^p$$

The vector $\vec{b}$ is called the **offset** of $f$
(statistics also calls it the *intercept*, and machine learning the *bias*).

For a real-valued function (@def-real-vector-valued, $m = 1$),
$\matr{A}$ is a single row, written $\vec{w}^\top$, and $\vec{b}$ is a single number $b$,
so an affine function is a linear function $\vec{w}^\top \vx$ (@cor-linear-scalar)
plus an offset:

$$f(\vx) = \vec{w}^\top \vx + b, \qquad \vec{w} \in \mathbb{R}^p, \quad b \in \mathbb{R}$$ {#eq-linear-scalar}

:::
